kicker: Power equipment · transformer makers' Q2 FY27 margins
title: Transformer margins are splitting by voltage
dek: Makers of 400 kV-plus units widened EBITDA margins in Q2 (Kanohar to 35%, TARIL +6.2 pt). Makers of lower-voltage units gave margin back as copper and steel costs went only partly to buyers.

read: Pricing power now sits at 400 kV and above; the test is whether new capacity and slower awards spread the squeeze upward.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 20 Nov 2026
notes: EBITDA margins from filed Q2 FY27 results (TARIL and Atlanta consolidated; GE Vernova T&D, Voltamp, Shilchar and Kanohar standalone). Kanohar listed recently and has no year-ago filing on the desk, so its Q2 FY26 margin (≈27.8%) is derived from the revenue (+112%) and EBITDA (+167%) growth stated on its call. Voltage grouping follows the companies' calls and the sector note (TARIL 55–60% of book at 400 kV-plus; Atlanta about 47% at 220 kV; Voltamp, which held no call, is grouped by the note). TARIL's standalone margin, cited on its call, was 16.1% vs 8.8%. Hitachi Energy India had not reported Q2.
